result.question: Town planning was the most distinctive feature of Harappan cities. Discuss. (Answer in 150 words)

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.

sentences.text: The Harappan Civilisation was marked by planned urban centres such as Mohenjodaro, Harappa, Dholavira and Lothal.
Mohenjodaro was divided into a raised, walled Citadel built on mud-brick platforms and a larger, separately walled Lower Town.
Its streets followed an approximate grid pattern, intersecting at right angles.
A carefully planned drainage system linked house drains to covered street drains, with sumps for cleaning.
Bricks, whether sun-dried or baked, followed a standardised ratio across Harappan settlements.
Houses were built around courtyards, had their own bathrooms and showed concern for privacy, with no windows in ground-level walls.
The Great Bath, a watertight tank probably used for ritual bathing, stood in the Lower Town among ordinary houses.
A massive granary, which some scholars call a warehouse, shows the ability to mobilise labour.
At Dholavira and Lothal the entire settlement was fortified.
Such planning suggests strong civic authority, and Harappan drainage still offers lessons for sanitation in modern cities.
